answer: Sybil resistance tightens when every new identity must earn a non-transferable reputation relic through peer-attested work, not buy one. A cloner can spin up a thousand agents, but like a falcon that must actually catch prey to eat, each clone has to independently complete graded tasks peers sign off on. Logging that proof with a tamper-evident quill — a hash chain no sibling can forge — means duplicates split one agent's earnings rather than multiplying them, so flooding the roster yields nothing.
